products.note: Enterprise content AI; metadata; governance; compliance; retention policies

reading.body:
Box has built a portfolio of integrations that let AI agents handle real-world tasks: sending physical mail, managing cloud files, accessing bank data, and exchanging secrets between agents.

These Model Context Protocol tools sit at the boundary between AI systems and the infrastructure they need to operate at scale. An AI agent that can only think cannot process a loan application or onboard an employee. It must read files, verify identity, send documents, and maintain audit trails. Box's integrations bridge this gap by giving agents standardized access to storage, communication channels, and cross-agent coordination. The company's own AI product focuses on enterprise content, but this MCP registry strategy positions it as an operational layer for agentic workflows, where the binding constraint shifts from model capability to the ability to act on real data and systems.

What these integrations do not show is compute or power consumption. They are software abstractions that assume infrastructure exists elsewhere. They do show that AI scaling now depends not only on larger models and more training compute, but on standardized ways for agents to access the human-world interfaces they need to do work. For enterprises, this means the grid constraint on AI is mediated through the systems that connect agents to email, filesystems, banks, and each other.

profile_text.body:
Box describes itself as an AI-powered content management, workflow, and collaboration platform. Its Intelligent Content Management platform is presented as a way to automate workflows, collaborate internally and externally, and protect sensitive data. The company's site says Box AI lets users tap into leading AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google for real-time summaries, deep analysis, and smart recommendations. It also describes AI-driven security, deep learning-based malware detection, automated classification, and compliance tools for GDPR, HIPAA, and FINRA.

Box AI is listed as an enterprise content AI product with metadata, governance, compliance, and retention policies. The site also mentions Box AI Studio for customizing agents and building workflows, and says it offers AI-driven e-signature workflows with unlimited e-signatures for free. According to the website, Box was named a Leader, with the highest scores possible in 13 criteria such as innovation, vision, security, AI/ML (including generative AI), and more.

Box is a for-profit public company founded in 2005 and headquartered in Redwood City, CA, USA, trading as BOX with CIK 0001372612. For the fiscal period ended 2026-01-31, Box reported revenue of $1,177,253,000 in a 10-K filing. Box is associated with 281 California law exposure entries and eight MCP server entries, including ai.clize/inbox, ai.ironshard/agent-storage-sandbox, and ai.powerline/inbox-preview.
